EU fragrance allergen disclosure list (Regulation 1223/2009); sensitization documented. Grade dim normalized allerg:D -> derm:D (schema fix, 2026-09-17): 'allerg' is not a canonical grade dimension; H317 sensitizer severity is carried in derm, matching Citral/Limonene/Fragrance. Allergenicity remains tagged in impacts.

Methylchloroisothiazolinone.s: CMIT — the chlorine half of the CMIT/MIT preservative pair. Corrosive, toxic if swallowed or in contact with skin, strong skin sensitizer, very toxic to aquatic life.
reclassified: CMIT/MIT (Kathon) was the workhorse preservative of the 1990s–2000s; an epidemic of contact allergy made it the archetype of 'the preservative is the hazard', now restricted in EU leave-on products.
Methylchloroisothiazolinone.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 33344): H314 98.3%, H317 98.4%, H400 94.5%, H410 40.3% consensus. Paired with Methylisothiazolinone (MIT) at ~3:1 in the common preservative blend.

Sodium Metasilicate.s: Alkaline silicate builder. Corrosive to skin and eyes; dust is a respiratory irritant.
Sodium Metasilicate.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 23266, disodium metasilicate / 'Sodium Silicate'): H314 >99.9%, H335 98.6%, H318 61.5%, H315 72.6% consensus. Dataset has a separate 'Sodium Silicate' entry (alkaline builder, H314,H335) — kept distinct because this is the metasilicate CAS 6834-92-0 used as a hard-surface builder.

Tetrasodium EDTA.s: Chelating agent (binds hard-water metals). Harmful if swallowed; serious eye damage; may damage organs on prolonged exposure.
Tetrasodium EDTA.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 6144, 'Edetate Sodium'): H318 >99.9%, H302 >99.9%, H335 56.3%, H315 58.1% consensus. EDTA's environmental concern is chelation/metal mobilisation rather than direct aquatic toxicity; the H-code block shows no H4xx.

Sodium Lauroyl Sarcosinate.s: Amino-acid (sarcosinate) surfactant. Serious eye damage and skin irritation; H330 (fatal if inhaled) reflects the aerosolisable powder form.
Sodium Lauroyl Sarcosinate.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 23668817): H315 83.7%, H318 79.8%, H330 81.9% consensus. Route caveat: H330 is a property of the inhalable powder/aerosol, not of the diluted liquid cleaner in which this appears; the respiratory F grade is form-conditional, applied per the house >=40% rule.

Sodium Benzoate.s: Preservative / corrosion inhibitor. Causes serious eye irritation.
Sodium Benzoate.note: ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 517055): H319 at 37.9% consensus — below the house's strict >=40% consensus bar for graded dims, so the grade is carried by precedent (Citric Acid / H319 -> derm C, eye-route irritation) rather than the consensus rule. Intentional food-grade preservative; low systemic hazard.

Acrylic Copolymer.s: High-molecular-weight acrylic film-former / anti-redeposition agent. No discrete PubChem CID.
Acrylic Copolymer.note: Polymer/UVCB — PubChem name lookup resolves no CID and therefore no GHS classification. Recorded as unclassified rather than assigned an unsourced grade: high-MW polymers are generally not bioavailable. Disclosed by Reckitt SmartLabel for Resolve.

Amino-Functional Silicone.s: Silicone antifoam / surface modifier. Polymeric; no discrete PubChem CID.
Amino-Functional Silicone.note: Polymer/UVCB — no PubChem GHS classification available. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed. Disclosed by Reckitt SmartLabel for Resolve. Distinct from 'Dimethicone' (non-functional PDMS).

Polyglyceryl-2 Oleate.s: Non-ionic emulsifier (polyglycerol ester of oleic acid).
Polyglyceryl-2 Oleate.note: No PubChem CID / GHS classification found for this UVCB ester. Recorded unclassified rather than assigned an unsourced grade. Disclosed by Weiman for Stainless Steel Cleaner & Polish.

Alcohols, C9-11, ethoxylated.s: Non-ionic alcohol ethoxylate surfactant (CAS 68439-46-3 / 160875-66-1). Supplier SDS classifies H318 (serious eye damage), H302, H335.
Alcohols, C9-11, ethoxylated.note: UVCB — no PubChem CID, so no ECHA consensus percentages are available. Grade extrapolated conservatively from the Rust-Oleum Krud Kutter SDS classification block (H318, H302, H335 at 1.0-2.5% in the product) and class-typical behaviour for C9-11 alcohol ethoxylates. Pending verification; NOT a consensus-derived grade.

Mineral Oil.s: White mineral oil (CAS 8042-47-5). Aspiration hazard if liquid reaches the airways; highly refined white oils are not classified carcinogenic.
Mineral Oil.note: Aspiration-only hazard (H304, Asp. Tox. 1) per the Weiman SDS composition block; ECHA treats highly refined white mineral oils as not classified for carcinogenicity. No dermal/respiratory grade applies to normal surface-cleaning exposure, so gr is deliberately empty rather than padded.

C11-15 Alkane/Cycloalkane.s: Petroleum hydrocarbon distillate solvent (CAS 64742-47-8, hydrotreated light distillate). Aspiration hazard.
C11-15 Alkane/Cycloalkane.note: Asp. Tox. 1 / H304 per the Weiman SDS composition block (CAS 64742-47-8 listed 10-15%). Hydrocarbon distillate; the hazard is aspiration on ingestion, not surface use. gr left empty deliberately.

Liquefied Petroleum Gas.s: LPG propellant (butane/propane mix, CAS 68476-85-7). Extremely flammable gas.
Liquefied Petroleum Gas.note: Physical hazard only — H220 (extremely flammable gas) per supplier SDS; no health-hazard grade applies. Propellant in the aerosol, not a cleaning active. The dataset already carries Butane and Propane separately.

Hexoxyethanol.s: Glycol ether (2-(hexyloxy)ethanol). Corrosive to skin and eyes in concentrate; toxic in contact with skin; combustible liquid.
Hexoxyethanol.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 8170, glycol monohexyl ether): H314 99.5%, H302 99.5%, H318 59.9%, H311 58.9%, H312 40.6% consensus; H227/H315/H320/H371 listed without a consensus percentage. Disclosed by Clorox SmartLabel for Disinfecting Wipes.

Triethanolamine.s: Ethanolamine. Skin/eye irritant and skin sensitizer; pH buffer and emulsifier in detergents.
Triethanolamine.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 7618): H317 (skin sensitizer) and H315 listed without a consensus percentage; H319 appears at 18.5% consensus, below the house >=40% bar, so the derm grade rests on H317/H315. Disclosed by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

BHT.s: Synthetic antioxidant preservative (butylated hydroxytoluene). Skin sensitizer; suspected reproductive toxicant; very toxic to aquatic life.
BHT.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 31404, 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol): H410 84.3%, H400 42.6% consensus; H361/H370/H373/H317 listed without a consensus percentage. Preservative in Woolite Delicates.

Butylphenyl Methylpropional.s: Synthetic lily-of-the-valley fragrance (Lilial). CMR-classified reproductive toxicant; strong skin sensitizer; banned in EU cosmetics since 2022.
reclassified: Lilial was a ubiquitous 'clean' floral scent note. Reclassified as a CMR reproductive toxicant (H360Fd) and banned in EU cosmetics in 2022 (Reg. 2022/1181) — yet it is still disclosed in some US cleaning products, with no equivalent US federal restriction.
Butylphenyl Methylpropional.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 228987, Lilial): H302 98.7%, H317 99.6%, H315 90.9%, H361 84.9%, H411 84.2% consensus; H360Fd appears at 10.9%, below the >=40% bar, but H361 (84.9%) carries the repro flag. Disclosed as a fragrance component by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

Hexyl Salicylate.s: Fragrance component (salicylate ester). Skin sensitizer; suspected developmental toxicant; very toxic to aquatic life.
Hexyl Salicylate.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 22629): H410 100%, H317 98.4%, H400 90.2% consensus; H315 (26.9%) and H319 (13.2%) are below the >=40% bar. Disclosed as a fragrance component by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

Isoeugenol.s: Fragrance component (isomer of eugenol). Skin sensitizer; suspected carcinogen; harmful if swallowed or in contact with skin.
Isoeugenol.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 853433): H317 99.7%, H302 99.5%, H315 99.5%, H319 98.9%, H312 96.4%, H335 53%, H332 52.3% consensus; H351/H371/H373 listed without a consensus percentage. Disclosed as a fragrance component by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

Eugenol.s: Fragrance component (clove oil constituent). Strong skin sensitizer; suspected carcinogen; toxic to aquatic life.
Eugenol.note: Graded from ECHA C&L via PubChem (CID 3314): H317 99.8%, H319 80.4% consensus; H302 (17.3%) and H315 (20.6%) are below the >=40% bar. Disclosed as a fragrance component by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

Sodium Polycarboxylate.s: Polymeric dispersant / anti-redeposition agent. No discrete PubChem CID.
Sodium Polycarboxylate.note: Polymer/UVCB — no PubChem entry for CAS 68479-09-4 (PUG REST 404). Recorded unclassified rather than guessed. Listed in the Church & Dwight SDS for OxiClean Versatile Stain Remover.

Formaldehyde-Melamine-Sodium Bisulfite C.s: Melamine-formaldehyde foam polymer (Magic Eraser abrasive). Polymeric; no discrete PubChem CID.
Formaldehyde-Melamine-Sodium Bisulfite C.note: Polymer/UVCB — no PubChem CID. P&G's SDS classifies the finished Magic Eraser as 'Not Classified' (no hazardous ingredients listed); the copolymer identity comes from the P&G MSDS composition section (reproduced in university chemical-safety listings). Recorded unclassified rather than guessed; the melamine-formaldehyde class is why it is tracked at all.

Alkyl C12-18 Dimethylbenzyl Ammonium Chl.s: Quaternary ammonium disinfectant (BAC-type). Class hazards: corrosive, aquatic toxicity, respiratory/allergic sensitization.
Alkyl C12-18 Dimethylbenzyl Ammonium Chl.note: UVCB quaternary-ammonium blend (CAS 53516-76-0) — no discrete PubChem CID. Graded by class analogy to the existing 'Benzalkonium Chloride'/'Quaternary Ammonium' entries (derm F, env F, allerg/resp); kept as its own record so the Clorox Wipes disclosure stays traceable. No invented grade.

Alkyl C12-14 Dimethylethylbenzyl Ammoniu.s: Quaternary ammonium disinfectant (BAC-type). Class hazards: corrosive, aquatic toxicity, respiratory/allergic sensitization.
Alkyl C12-14 Dimethylethylbenzyl Ammoniu.note: UVCB quaternary-ammonium blend (CAS 85409-23-0) — no discrete PubChem CID. Graded by class analogy to the existing 'Benzalkonium Chloride'/'Quaternary Ammonium' entries; kept as its own record for traceability. No invented grade.

TEA Cocoate.s: Coconut-oil-derived triethanolamine soap (surfactant). UVCB; no discrete PubChem CID.
TEA Cocoate.note: UVCB (CAS 61790-64-5) — no PubChem entry (PUG REST 404). Soap-type anionic surfactant; recorded unclassified/extrapolated rather than assigned an invented grade. Disclosed by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

C10-16 Pareth.s: Alcohol ethoxylate surfactant (C10-16 pareth). UVCB; no discrete PubChem CID.
C10-16 Pareth.note: UVCB (CAS 68002-97-1) — no PubChem entry. Class-analogous to the existing 'Ethoxylated Alcohol'/'Alcohol Ethoxylate' entries (derm C, env C; trace 1,4-dioxane from ethoxylation). Recorded extrapolated, not graded. Disclosed by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

C12-14 Alcohols Ethoxylated Propoxylated.s: Alcohol ethoxylate/propoxylate surfactant (low-foam). UVCB; no discrete PubChem CID.
C12-14 Alcohols Ethoxylated Propoxylated.note: UVCB — no PubChem CID. Class-analogous to 'Ethoxylated Alcohol'. Recorded extrapolated rather than graded. Disclosed by Clorox SmartLabel for Disinfecting Wipes.

Sodium (C10-16) Alkylbenzenesulfonate.s: Linear alkylbenzene sulfonate (LAS) surfactant. UVCB; class hazards: skin/eye irritant, aquatic toxicity.
Sodium (C10-16) Alkylbenzenesulfonate.note: UVCB (CAS 68081-81-2) — no PubChem entry. Class-analogous to the existing 'Sodium Dodecylbenzenesulfonate' entry (derm D, env C). Recorded extrapolated, not graded. Disclosed by Reckitt SmartLabel for Woolite Delicates.

Laureth-12.s: Fatty-alcohol ethoxylate surfactant (lauryl alcohol + 12 EO). Causes serious eye damage in concentrate.
Laureth-12.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 76460): H318 100% consensus, H302 100%. PubChem name lookup returned a matching title ('Laureth-12').

Fatty Acids, C8-18 and C18-Unsaturated S.s: Sodium soaps of C8-18 fatty acids (UVCB). Mild irritants at use levels; no GHS classification available for the mixture.
Fatty Acids, C8-18 and C18-Unsaturated S.note: UVCB (CAS 67701-30-8). PubChem PUG REST returns 404 for both the name and the CAS — no discrete CID and therefore no GHS classification. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed, matching the house treatment of polymer/UVCB entries (see 'Acrylic Copolymer').

Polyethyleneimine Alkoxylated.s: Polymeric dispersant / anti-redeposition agent (UVCB). No discrete PubChem CID.
Polyethyleneimine Alkoxylated.note: Polymer/UVCB — PubChem name lookup resolves no CID (PUG REST 404) and therefore no GHS classification. Recorded unclassified rather than assigned an unsourced grade; high-MW polymers are generally not bioavailable. Disclosed by Henkel SmartLabel for Persil ProClean.

Sodium Metaborate.s: Borate salt (boron compound). EU/CLP-classified reproductive toxicant 1B (H360FD); eye irritant.
reclassified: Borates were long treated as benign 'mineral' builders. EU CLP harmonized them as Reproductive toxicant 1B (H360FD); ECHA RAC confirmed the classification in 2014. US still allows them in household products off the shelf.
Sodium Metaborate.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 145326): H360FD (harmonized borates group classification), H361 68.5% consensus, H319 52.6% consensus. Mirrors the existing 'Sodium Tetraborate' entry (also borates, repro F). Industry SDS literature notes sodium metaborate dihydrate is Repr. 2 (H361d) with a >=9.1% specific concentration limit; the harmonized group classification is the stricter 1B.

Tetrasodium Iminodisuccinate.s: Biodegradable chelating agent (aspartic acid derivative). No GHS hazard criteria met.
Tetrasodium Iminodisuccinate.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 9927753): 'Reported as not meeting GHS hazard criteria by 231 of 231 companies.' One of the few chelators with a unanimous clean verdict.

Hydrophobically Modified Acrylate/Styren.s: Polymeric structurant / thickener (UVCB). No discrete PubChem CID.
Hydrophobically Modified Acrylate/Styren.note: Polymer/UVCB — PubChem name lookup resolves no CID (PUG REST 404) and therefore no GHS classification. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed.

Disodium Distyrylbiphenyl Disulfonate.s: Fluorescent whitening agent (stilbene disulfonate type). Eye irritant.
Disodium Distyrylbiphenyl Disulfonate.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 33786): H319 74% consensus -> derm C; H318 25% (below the 40% house threshold, so it does not drive a D grade).

Polyoxyalkylene Substituted Chromophore.s: Polymeric colorant (the 'Blue' in the SmartLabel disclosure). No discrete PubChem CID.
Polyoxyalkylene Substituted Chromophore.note: Polymer/UVCB — no PubChem entry for this trade description. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed.

Mannanase Enzyme.s: Mannan-degrading detergent enzyme. Enzyme proteins are respiratory sensitizers by class.
Mannanase Enzyme.note: No PubChem CID (PUG VIEW 404). Extrapolated by enzyme class, consistent with the existing 'Enzymes' and 'Amylase Enzyme' entries — detergent enzyme proteins are respiratory sensitizers (H334 class hazard). Flagged for verification.

Cellulase Enzyme.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 440950): H334 99.4% consensus.

Myristamine Oxide.s: Amine oxide surfactant (myristyl dimethyl amine oxide). Serious eye damage; very toxic to aquatic life.
Myristamine Oxide.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 18739): H318 100%, H315 95.5%, H400 92.2%, H302 78.2% consensus.

Sodium Chlorate.s: Strong oxidizer; toxic if swallowed; toxic to aquatic life with long-lasting effects.
reclassified: Sodium chlorate is not added to bleach cleaners — it forms as the hypochlorite decays in storage (3 NaOCl -> NaClO3 + 2 NaCl). It appears on the label as a disclosed component of Clorox Clean-Up.
Sodium Chlorate.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 516902): H411 98.9% -> env D; H271 100% strong oxidizer (physical hazard, not a health dimension); H301/H302 acute oral toxicity. Chlorate formation from stored hypochlorite is documented in the OxyChem Sodium Hypochlorite Handbook and Olin's Sodium Hypochlorite Product Stewardship Manual.

Benzophenone.s: Photoinitiator / UV stabilizer; classified as a suspected human carcinogen (H350, IARC 2B).
reclassified: Benzophenone is prohibited in EU cosmetics (Annex II, Entry 1703) yet appears on the US disclosure label of a household bleach spray cleaner — where the cosmetics ban does not reach.
Benzophenone.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 3102): H350 (harmonized Carc. 1B, 'May cause cancer') and H351; H373 37.4% -> organ C; H411 74.8% -> env D. Clorox SmartLabel flags it with the DL symbol (California Cleaning Products Right to Know designated list).

Sodium Orthosilicate.s: Alkaline silicate builder. Corrosive to skin and eyes; dust is a respiratory irritant.
Sodium Orthosilicate.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 26051): H314 100%, H335 100% consensus.

Isopropanolamine.s: Corrosive alkanolamine; harmful in contact with skin.
Isopropanolamine.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 4, '1-Amino-2-propanol'): H314 >99.9%, H318 87.5%, H312 83.7% consensus.

Tartaric Acid.s: Food acid (the acid in grapes/wine). Skin and eye irritant; a contact allergen in sensitised people.
Tartaric Acid.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 444305, 'L-Tartaric acid'): H315 54.3%, H319 57.8%, H317 42.5%, H318 41.2%, H335 55.4% consensus. ECHA C&L notifier consensus is unusually harsh for a GRAS food acid — recorded as reported rather than softened.

Formic Acid.s: Corrosive acid; pH adjuster in fabric softeners.
Formic Acid.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 284): H314 99.7% -> derm F; H226 21.1% combustible liquid; H318 19.2%, H331 17.9%, H302 18.3% all below the 40% house threshold and therefore not graded. In Downy Free & Gentle it is a trace pH adjuster, not a cleaning agent.

Pentasodium Pentetate.s: Chelating agent (penta-sodium DTPA). Harmful if inhaled; EU/CLP consensus flags reproductive/developmental concern.
Pentasodium Pentetate.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 8779): H332 87.7% -> resp C; H361 67.4% -> repro D; H360D 18.5% (below threshold) and H373 31.3% (below threshold).

Diethylester Dimethyl Ammonium Chloride.s: Biodegradable ester-quat fabric softener active (DEEDMAC). Class hazards: skin/eye irritation, aquatic toxicity.
Diethylester Dimethyl Ammonium Chloride.note: UVCB (CAS 919-30-2). PubChem returns no CID for the name (PUG REST 404). Recorded extrapolated by quat class rather than invented — the class hazards are skin/eye irritation and aquatic toxicity (see the existing 'Quaternary Ammonium' entry).

Polyquaternium-33.s: Polymeric stabilizer (UVCB). No discrete PubChem CID.
Polyquaternium-33.note: Polymer/UVCB — PubChem name lookup resolves no CID (PUG REST 404) and therefore no GHS classification. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed.

Calcium Chloride.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 5284359): headline ECHA C&L block reports H319 at 99.7% notifier consensus (eye irritant -> derm C). Secondary blocks add H318, H302, H335 and H373, all below the >=40% consensus threshold and so not graded. Disclosed by Reckitt for Spray 'n Wash.

Potassium Chloride.s: No GHS hazard criteria met (majority not-classified per ECHA C&L via PubChem)
Potassium Chloride.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 4873): 825 of 875 companies (94.3%) report not meeting GHS hazard criteria. Disclosed by Reckitt for Spray 'n Wash.

Diisopropanolamine.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 8086): headline ECHA C&L block reports H318 at 51.2% consensus (serious eye damage -> derm D). A secondary block reports H314 (severe skin burns) but below the >=40% consensus threshold, so not graded. Disclosed by SC Johnson for fantastik.

Sodium Polyacrylate.s: Polymeric dispersant / anti-redeposition agent (UVCB). No discrete PubChem CID.
Sodium Polyacrylate.note: Polymer/UVCB (CAS 9003-04-7) - PubChem name lookup resolves no CID (PUG REST 404) and therefore no GHS classification. Recorded unclassified rather than assigned an unsourced grade; high-MW polymers are generally not bioavailable. Disclosed by Henkel for Purex Free & Clear and by Reckitt for Spray 'n Wash.

Fluorescent Brightener 28.s: Optical brightener (stilbene disulfonate dye). No GHS hazard criteria met.
Fluorescent Brightener 28.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 6434593, title 'Cellufluor' - a synonym of Calcofluor White / Fluorescent Brightener 28, CAS 4193-55-9): 268 of 274 companies (97.8%) report not meeting GHS hazard criteria. Disclosed by Henkel for Purex Free & Clear.

Protease Enzyme.s: Protein-degrading detergent enzyme. Enzyme proteins are respiratory sensitizers by class.
Protease Enzyme.note: No PubChem CID for the generic label term 'Protease' - the name lookup returns an unrelated compound (Bacillomycin, CID 3086051) which is not used. Extrapolated by enzyme class, consistent with the existing 'Subtilisin', 'Amylase Enzyme' and 'Cellulase Enzyme' entries - detergent protease proteins are respiratory sensitizers (H334 class hazard). Disclosed by Reckitt for Spray 'n Wash.

PEI-14 PEG-24/PPG-16 Copolymer.s: Polymeric dispersant / anti-redeposition agent (UVCB). No discrete PubChem CID.
PEI-14 PEG-24/PPG-16 Copolymer.note: Polymer/UVCB - PubChem name lookup resolves no CID and therefore no GHS classification. Recorded unclassified rather than assigned an unsourced grade. Disclosed by P&G SmartLabel for Ivory Concentrated Dishwashing Liquid.

Petroleum Distillates, Hydrotreated Ligh.note: UVCB petroleum stream (CAS 64742-47-8). PubChem PUG REST returns 404 for both the CAS and the descriptive name - no discrete CID, therefore no GHS classification is assigned. Manufacturer SDS (Goo Gone, rev. 9/19/2024) classifies Asp. Tox. 1 (H304, aspiration hazard if swallowed) - aspiration hazard is outside the graded dimensions, so no dimension grade is set. Disclosed by Goo Gone for Goo Gone Original.

Orange Oil.s: Citrus terpene oil - aspiration hazard, skin sensitizer, serious eye damage, aquatic toxicity.
Orange Oil.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 62161, title 'Orange Oil'): dominant ECHA C&L block (10 notifications / 262 reports) reports H304 89.7%, H315 90.5%, H317 90.5% (skin sensitization -> derm D + allerg), H318 44.7% (serious eye damage -> derm D), H411 90.1% (aquatic long-term -> env D). H226 (flammable liquid) at 39.7% falls below the >=40% consensus threshold and is not graded. Disclosed by Goo Gone for Goo Gone Original.

Aliphatic Ether Alcohol.s: Solvent disclosed by generic class name only; identity withheld.
Aliphatic Ether Alcohol.note: Name withheld by the manufacturer as a trade secret - no CAS, no discrete identity and no PubChem CID, so no classification is possible. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed. Disclosed on the Goo Gone Original ingredient list.

Glycol Ether.s: Solvent disclosed by generic class name only; identity withheld.
Glycol Ether.note: Name withheld by the manufacturer as a trade secret - no CAS, no discrete identity and no PubChem CID, so no classification is possible. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed. Disclosed on the Goo Gone Original ingredient list. Note the glycol-ether class carries reproductive/developmental concern in EU/Prop 65 classifications (see 'Diethylene Glycol Monobutyl Ether'), but the specific substance here is not identified and no class grade is assigned.

Solvent Orange 60.s: Orange dye colorant; no GHS hazard criteria met.
Solvent Orange 60.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 81344, title 'Solvent Orange 60'): 2229 of 2274 companies (98.0%) report not meeting GHS hazard criteria. Disclosed by Goo Gone for Goo Gone Original.

Tripropylene Glycol Butyl Ether.s: Glycol ether solvent (PPG-3 butyl ether); no GHS hazard classification in PubChem.
Tripropylene Glycol Butyl Ether.note: PubChem CID 60196418 (title 'Tripropylene glycol n-butyl ether') carries no GHS Classification section, so no H-codes are available. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed. Disclosed by SC Johnson for Shout Advanced Stain Remover.

Polyester Sheet.s: Substrate material (nonwoven polyester carrier sheet), not a chemical substance.
Polyester Sheet.note: The dryer-sheet substrate itself, disclosed as a material rather than a substance. No CAS, no PubChem CID and no GHS classification applies. Disclosed by P&G for Bounce Fabric Softener Sheets.

Dialkylester Dimethyl Ammonium Methosulf.s: Quaternary ammonium fabric-softener active, disclosed by generic class name.
Dialkylester Dimethyl Ammonium Methosulf.note: Proprietary quaternary ammonium softener active disclosed only by generic class name - no CAS and no discrete PubChem CID, so no classification is assigned. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed. Disclosed by P&G for Bounce Fabric Softener Sheets.

Fatty Acids, C16-18 and C18-unsatd..s: Fatty acid blend (UVCB) used as a softener carrier.
Fatty Acids, C16-18 and C18-unsatd..note: UVCB (CAS 67701-37-5 region). PubChem PUG REST resolves no discrete CID for the blend, therefore no GHS classification. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed, matching the house treatment of UVCB entries (see 'Fatty Acids, C8-18 and C18-Unsaturated Sodium Salts'). Disclosed by P&G for Bounce Fabric Softener Sheets.

Bentonite.s: Mineral clay (montmorillonite) used as a softener carrier.
Bentonite.note: Mineral clay (CAS 1302-78-9). PubChem PUG REST returns 404 for the name - no discrete CID resolved, therefore no GHS classification is assigned. Recorded unclassified rather than guessed. Respirable crystalline silica is a separate concern that depends on the specific grade's quartz content, which is not disclosed on the label. Disclosed by P&G for Bounce Fabric Softener Sheets.

Undeceth-3.s: Ethoxylated undecyl alcohol surfactant - harmful if swallowed, serious eye damage.
Undeceth-3.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 61930, title '2-Undecyloxy-1-ethanol'): two single-company ECHA C&L notifications (1 notification each) report H302 100% and H318 100% (serious eye damage -> derm D), plus H319 100%. Low confidence because the denominator is one company per notification. Note the CID is the mono-ethoxylate homolog while Undeceth-3 denotes the 3-EO homolog - the CAS 34398-01-1 covers the ethoxylated undecyl alcohol family. Disclosed by The Works for The Works Toilet Bowl Cleaner.

Methenamine.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 4101, title 'Hexamethylenetetramine' - a synonym of methenamine): the dominant ECHA C&L block (19 notifications / 1051 reports) reports H317 100% (skin sensitization -> derm C + allerg) and H228 100% (flammable solid, a physical hazard outside the graded dimensions). A second block from only 2 notifications reports H302/H314/H334/H351 at 100% - a 2-notification fringe whose percentages are within-group, not global consensus, so those are NOT graded here. Disclosed by The Works for The Works Toilet Bowl Cleaner.

Sapindus Saponins.s: No harmonised GHS classification located for the saponin extract
Sapindus Saponins.note: The triterpenoid saponins of Sapindus mukorossi are the surfactant in soap nuts. No harmonised GHS classification exists and the toxicology is thin, so this is recorded as no-classification with weak evidence rather than graded: grading a substance with no harmonised classification would be invention. What the literature does say, and it cuts both ways: the saponins reduce water surface tension below 40 mN/m and match a commercial detergent on greasy and oily soil, while a 2023 wastewater study found soapnut effluent acutely more toxic to zebrafish than commercial detergent, with saponin degradation slow enough that treatment matters. Compare Quillaja Saponaria Bark Extract, which carries the same grading gap.
